children: Oppenheimer initiated coverage of FuelCell Energy

with an Outperform rating and a $24 price target, arguing that surging power requirements from data centers could create a major growth opportunity for the fuel-cell equipment maker. The target compares with a share price of $16.49 cited in the report.
Lead analyst Colin Rusch said FuelCell

is positioned to provide on-site, behind-the-meter electricity for data centers that face delays connecting to the power grid. The company plans to increase annual production capacity from roughly 40 megawatts to 100 MW around the end of fiscal 2026 and 500 MW by fiscal 2029.
Oppenheimer sees evidence that demand is already developing. FuelCell

exited its fiscal third quarter with a sales pipeline exceeding 10 gigawatts, roughly 97% of which was tied to data centers. Its pipeline grew more than sixfold from the fiscal first quarter, while the average proposed project expanded to more than 200 MW.

That interest has begun turning into orders. FuelCell reached an agreement with Fit Energy for as much as 380 MW, starting with 30 MW for initial delivery in calendar 2026, and subsequently signed a capacity reservation agreement covering as much as 75 MW with another data center customer.

For investors, the central question is whether FuelCell can convert that demand into enough volume to transform its economics. Oppenheimer forecasts revenue rising from $158 million in fiscal 2025 to $397 million in fiscal 2028 and $932 million in fiscal 2030. Gross margins are expected to turn positive in the second half of fiscal 2027, with EBITDA becoming positive in fiscal 2028 and reaching about $78 million by fiscal 2030.

The analysts also see FuelCell's balance sheet providing room to finance the expansion. The company had $658 million of unrestricted cash following a $245 million equity raise in July, alongside $1.30 billion of committed backlog and $2.35 billion of awarded backlog. Oppenheimer estimates the Torrington, Connecticut, manufacturing expansion will cost $200 million to $275 million.

Oppenheimer's $24 target is based on four times its fiscal 2030 revenue estimate of $932 million, discounted back two years at 10%. The firm's assumptions also account for dilution from stock compensation and warrants issued to Fit Energy.
The bullish case carries substantial execution risk. FuelCell

remains unprofitable and must successfully expand manufacturing while converting its pipeline into firm orders. Oppenheimer also flags potential shareholder dilution, dependence on fuel-cell tax credits, competition and technology risks. The 12 million Fit Energy warrants alone could represent roughly 13% dilution to the current share count.
